summary: The article surveys school initiatives that build global citizenship and multicultural awareness, from curriculum changes and language offerings to exchange programs, virtual exchanges, teacher training, community projects, sustainability, arts and debate. Each initiative is tied to a named school and educator. It concludes that systemic changes toward global education standards are still ongoing.
one_line: Overview of school programs across the country, from Global Studies to virtual exchanges, that foster global citizenship and multicultural awareness in students.
key_facts: Jackson High School introduced its Global Studies program late last year, spearheaded by Dr. Lydia Hoffman, who is known for her international teaching experience.
Mandarin, Spanish, French and less commonly taught languages like Swahili are now part of core offerings at some schools; Michael Chen of Valley Magnet School says "Language is a cultural bridge."
Susan Patel, director of Pioneer Academy's international program, says immersive study abroad is how "global literacy is built."
Pioneer Academy has partnered with schools in over ten countries in an exchange program that prioritizes socio-economic diversity and inclusion.

Westwood Digital Prep launched the "Virtual Cultural Exchange" initiative on November 3, 2023, using virtual reality so students can 'visit' landmarks and join cultural festivals from their classroom.
Amina Yusuf, English teacher and head of the diversity committee at Fairview Middle School, launched an intercultural communication workshop for teachers and staff last December.
Crescent High launched "Neighborhood Narratives" on October 20, 2023, connecting students with local community leaders, artists and entrepreneurs.
Sterling Elementary introduced the "Global Guardians" program on Earth Day, April 22, 2024, in which students develop projects tackling environmental issues; Samantha Lee is the program coordinator.
"Harmony Without Borders," started in fall 2023, links student bands and art collectives from different countries through virtual collaborations; David Ortiz is music director at Melody Arts High.
By mid-September 2023 the National Perspectives Debate League (NPDL) had included global issues in its topics; coordinator Jane Smith says debate cultivates respect for diversity of thought.
Crescent High Principal Carlos Rodriguez says students are "not just citizens of the world but also dedicated members of their local communities."
The article states that systemic changes incorporating global education standards are ongoing and there is ample room for growth.
